standard.title: Share arts works with audiences
standard.description: share their arts works with audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have created simple movement sequences and arts works communicating personal ideas (AC9ADAFC01). They have some experience of physical play and movement exploration (AC9ADAFD01).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students share their arts works — including movement and dance — with audiences.

nodes.label: Being an audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate as an attentive audience for peers' arts works — watching, noticing, and responding.
nodes.minimum_width: Participating as audience for at least one class sharing event; using positive language to comment on a peer's work.
nodes.typical_width: Participating in class gallery or performance walks; observing peers' works with attention; using positive language to identify features — shapes, movements, patterns — and sharing observations with peers and teachers.
wider: Take and curate digital images of class arts events (with permission), sequencing them to document the occasion
Respond to peers' work through a different arts form — e.g. drawing a response image or creating a sound to accompany a movement

response_modes.reason: Students need repeated practice as audience members to build observational vocabulary and respectful viewing habits. Multiple sharing events across the year build this repertoire.

success_criteria: Student watches a peer's work with sustained attention
Student uses at least one positive, specific comment about a peer's work

nodes.label: Sharing with an audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can present a movement sequence or arts work to an audience of peers and/or teachers, communicating their idea through performance.
nodes.minimum_width: Presenting a movement/dance sequence they have created to the class — with a brief explanation of what their work is about.
nodes.typical_width: Performing or presenting arts works — movement sequences, songs, soundscapes, dramatic play — to peers; introducing the work by describing a favourite moment, explaining the idea, or responding to teacher questions about the work.
wider: Use a digital device to record their movement/arts exploration, creating an image sequence or video to share
Perform a movement/dance sequence created collaboratively with a peer or small group, introducing the shared work
nodes.hinge_reason: Sharing with an audience is the completing act of the creative cycle at Foundation — students who have not experienced presenting their work have not yet closed the loop between making and communicating. This is the foundation for all subsequent Presenting strand standards.

response_modes.reason: Presenting integrates all prior work — idea, movement vocabulary, sequencing — into a communicative act. Frame sharing as purposeful communication: 'What do you want your audience to see?', 'What will you tell them about your work?'

success_criteria: Student presents a movement sequence or arts work to at least a small audience of peers
Student can say something about their work when asked — what it is about, or what they enjoyed making
